subject: Dedicated capacity discovery recap — Equilibrium Finance
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Chen <alex.chen@equilibrium.ai>
Cc: Rafael Mendes <rafael.mendes@redwood.ai>, Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 14 Aug 2026 15:32:00 -0700
Subject: Dedicated capacity discovery recap — Equilibrium Finance

Alex — great to meet earlier. Quick recap from our call and agreed next steps to make sure we’re aligned before the technical deep-dive. Please reply with any corrections/omissions.

Pain points
- Large latency spikes at month-end reporting windows (95th/99th percentiles can double).
- Cost variability from bursty traffic and inefficient batching in current self-hosted stack.
- Security/regulatory need for isolation (financial data) and strict audit logs.

Current stack
- Inference hosted on GCP, mix of T4s for dev and a few A100s for heavy workloads.
- Using an internal OpenLLM-based serving layer + custom batching logic.
- Approx 120k inference requests/day; peak concurrency around 180 qps during close windows.

What success looks like (high level)
- Predictable throughput: dedicated capacity that can reliably sustain 150–200 qps with headroom for spikes to ~400 qps.
- Latency SLO: 90th percentile <200ms for our primary prompt mix.
- Isolation & compliance: VPC + customer-managed KMS, SOC2 evidence, detailed audit logs, and data retention controls.
- Cost: Reduce per-token unit cost by 20–30% vs current monthly spend while keeping quality.

Technical requirements we captured
- Region preference: us-east-1 for data residency and lowest latency to our infra.
- Preferred GPUs: open to A100 pools for critical models; discuss mixed pools for cost optimization.
- Autoscaling/burst: need both steady reserved capacity and burst lift to handle end-of-month spikes; target burst from baseline 200 qps -> 400 qps for up to 6 hours during close.
- KV/prefix caching: must preserve session context across requests; cache invalidation window should be configurable.

Next steps
1) Technical deep-dive with your infra/ML engineer and our solutions architect — propose Thu Aug 20 or Mon Aug 24, 11am–2pm ET.
2) Redwood to share: preliminary Dedicated capacity sizing + two pricing scenarios (baseline reserved + burst buffer) — see attached Redwood_Dedicated_Pricing_v1.pdf.
3) Draft a mutual action plan for procurement/timeline (attached mutual-action-plan.md).
4) Security questionnaire kickoff (Equilibrium security can send SOC2/KMS specifics) — we’ll loop PM/Legal if needed.

If that aligns, I’ll lock the tech deep-dive and kick off an internal capacity sizing with Rafael and Vanessa.

Thanks,
Marissa Cole
Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.ai | (415) 555-0123

Attachments: Redwood_Dedicated_Pricing_v1.pdf (pricing sketch), mutual-action-plan.md (MAP draft)

From: Alex Chen <alex.chen@equilibrium.ai>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Cc: Rafael Mendes <rafael.mendes@redwood.ai>, Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.ai>, security@equilibrium.ai
Date: Fri, 14 Aug 2026 16:04:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity discovery recap — Equilibrium Finance

Thanks Marissa — that looks right from our side. Couple clarifications/additions:
- Monthly volume: currently ~3.6M inference requests / month (varies), with ~10% month-over-month growth.
- Peak concurrency note: 180 qps is average peak last quarter; during close windows we saw short bursts up to ~420 qps but typically 4–6 hours total across those days.
- Model mix: two primary models in prod — a 13B instruction-tuned model for summarization and a smaller 7B for quick classification. We’d want options to pin different models to different pools.
- Security: SOC2 Type II report available; we need customer-managed KMS + VPC peering and at-rest encryption.

Tech deep-dive: Aug 20, 11:30am ET works for our infra lead (Samir Patel) — I’ll send a calendar invite. Please include anyone who will speak to autoscaling and burst policies.

Appreciate the pricing draft — I’ll review and share with procurement.

—Alex
Alex Chen
Head of ML Infrastructure | Equilibrium Finance
alex.chen@equilibrium.ai | (212) 555-0199

From: Rafael Mendes <rafael.mendes@redwood.ai>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.ai>
Date: Sat, 15 Aug 2026 08:12:00 -0700
Subject: Fwd: Dedicated capacity discovery recap — Equilibrium Finance

Forwarding Alex's reply so we have the peak numbers and model mix in-thread. Key asks for sizing:
- Baseline sustained: plan for 200 qps baseline (headroom to 250 qps).
- Burst windows: support 400–450 qps for up to 6 hours/day during month-end windows.
- Model pinning: need separate pools or pricing for pinned A100 capacity for the 13B model; 7B can run on mixed A10/A100.
- Region: us-east-1 preferred.

Action items for engineering sizing:
- Evaluate two configs: (A) 4xA100 nodes (larger per-node capacity, simpler) vs (B) mixed pool 8xA10 + 2xA100 for cost-flexibility.
- Estimate steady-state token throughput and expected cost per 1M tokens for both configs.
- Prepare notes on autoscaling approach: warm pool + instantaneous burst via reserved buffer vs on-demand spin-up latency.

I’ll pick up the initial cost estimates and want to sync with Infra Ops (Vanessa) to confirm region constraints and networking (VPC peering details).

-Rafael
VP, Solutions Engineering | Redwood Inference
